cards.front: Kernicterus is caused by the [___] fraction of bilirubin, which is lipid-soluble, poorly albumin-bound at high levels, and able to cross the neonatal blood-brain barrier.
cards.context:
This is the same fraction that rises in haemolysis (Rh/ABO, G6PD), which is why jaundice in the first 24 h is treated as a haemolytic emergency.

A raised conjugated (direct) fraction is a different problem — it does not cross the blood-brain barrier, is never physiological, and points to biliary atresia or neonatal hepatitis.

Trap: reading any neonatal jaundice as benign.

cards.front: In NSW, termination of pregnancy is available on request up to [___] weeks; beyond that requires two practitioners and a hospital setting.
cards.context:
The 22-week threshold in NSW (and most Australian states) reflects fetal viability and aligns with the legal framework when termination was decriminalised.

State-by-state variation: VIC allows on-request abortion to 24 weeks; QLD + SA cluster around 22 weeks.

 Since March 2024, WA allows abortion on request to 23 weeks; after 23 weeks two practitioners are required, and the former Ministerial Panel approval process has been abolished. Check current local legislation.

cards.front: Small for gestational age (SGA) = estimated fetal weight (EFW) <[___]th centile; fetal growth restriction (FGR) is pathological, usually below the 3rd centile or abnormal Dopplers.
cards.context:
The trap: SGA is a size label, FGR is a diagnosis of failed growth potential.

SGA just means EFW <10th centile. Many are constitutionally small but healthy (small parents, female fetus), needing only surveillance to confirm normal velocity with normal Dopplers.

FGR is the pathological subset, flagged by centile <3rd OR abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers signalling placental insufficiency. Doppler separates the at-risk fetus from the merely small one and drives delivery.

cards.front: A Bishop score of [___] means the cervix is favourable, so induction can start with amniotomy with or without oxytocin.
cards.context:
Bishop score quantifies cervical favourability for induction — five components: dilatation, effacement, station scored 0-3 each; consistency, position scored 0-2 each — max total 13.

Ripening options: prostaglandin (PGE2 dinoprostone gel/pessary, or misoprostol PGE1), cervical balloon (Foley or Cook), or membrane sweeping for borderline.

Failed induction is more common with low scores. Australian guidance ripens the cervix at 6 or less; US sources often quote 8 as the cut-off.

cards.front: At 23 weeks, a fetus develops hydrops and Doppler evidence of anaemia. Maternal antibody screening is negative. Several weeks earlier, the mother had arthralgia after her child developed a slapped-cheek rash. The most likely infecting virus is [___].
cards.context:
Parvovirus infects fetal erythroid precursors, reducing red-cell production and potentially causing high-output failure with hydrops.

The exposure and maternal arthralgia support infection; a negative red-cell antibody screen makes alloimmune haemolysis less likely.

cards.front: In suspected ovarian torsion, a normal colour Doppler does NOT exclude the diagnosis; proceed to [___] if clinical suspicion is high.
cards.context:
The Doppler trap in ovarian torsion is intermittent flow.

Time to detorsion drives ovarian salvage rates. Detorsion within 6-8 hours of symptom onset usually preserves the ovary; beyond 24 hours, necrosis is likely.

So when the clinical picture is right (sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain, peritonism, vomiting, adnexal mass on imaging) — go straight to laparoscopy.

cards.front: The single biggest risk factor for postpartum endometritis is route of birth: caesarean section; treatment is amoxicillin + gentamicin + [___].
cards.context:
Endometritis is polymicrobial bacterial infection of the endometrium + adjacent decidua.

Presentation: fever ≥38°C, lower abdominal/uterine tenderness, malodorous lochia, raised WCC.

Consider differentials (wound infection, retained products, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis).

cards.front: HPV vaccination prevents about [___]% of cervical cancers; cervical screening is still required because the vaccine misses the remaining oncogenic HPV types.
cards.context:
The nonavalent vaccine covers seven oncogenic types (16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, 58) plus the low-risk wart types 6 and 11.

Vaccinated women therefore still need screening to catch the residual risk.

The National Cervical Screening Program runs 5-yearly HPV testing from 25 to 74 regardless of vaccination; any oncogenic HPV gets reflex liquid-based cytology, and HPV 16/18 goes to colposcopy.

cards.front: Trial of labour after caesarean: baseline uterine rupture risk is approximately 0.5% in experienced centres; risk [___] with oxytocin augmentation. Overall TOLAC success rate is around 70%.
cards.context:
VBAC carries a small but real risk of uterine rupture along the previous scar — ~1:200 (0.5%) in experienced centres for a single previous transverse lower segment CS.

Risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation (over-stimulation stresses scar), rises with prior classical (vertical) incision (~5-10% — generally contraindicates VBAC), multiple previous CS.

VBAC success rate ~70%, lower without prior vaginal birth + recurrent CS indication.

cards.front: A pregnant woman asks her GP about treating nausea and vomiting with cannabis. She is advised against it: cannabis use in pregnancy is associated with preterm birth and [___].
cards.context: Cannabis, including medicinal cannabinoids, is not recommended during pregnancy.

cards.front: Jaundice appearing in the first 24 hours particularly raises concern for [___].
cards.context:
Jaundice before 24 hours is pathological until assessed; consider Rh/ABO haemolysis. Check maternal/baby blood groups, DAT, FBC/film, reticulocytes and serum bilirubin.

Use age-, gestation- and risk-specific treatment charts: phototherapy first, exchange transfusion at its threshold or for bilirubin encephalopathy. IV fluids support hydration; they do not replace treatment.
